messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: canary group 'release/2026-03-15' has crossed abort thresholds
infra-bot: metric: 5xx_rate=17.8% (3m window) | health_check_failures=12/120 | abort_criteria=true
Alice Chen: seeing the bot — I'm taking this. oncall here.
Alice Chen: which service? logs?
infra-bot: service: renderer-api-v2 / deployment: release-2026-03-15-canary-1
eng-release-bot: Canary deploy ID: r2026-03-15-7f2a started 4m ago. rollout at 12% traffic.
Raj Patel: +1 oncall. I'm pulling logs now. thinking: if abort criteria true we should flip the feature flag and throttle traffic back to stable.
Marta Gomez: confirm impact matrix? any premium customers hit?
Alice Chen: quick check -- s3 of request_ids show 503s and 502s from backend-transform during decode. sample log below:
```
[2026-03-15T22:14:02Z] request_id=abc123 route=/v1/generate status=502 duration_ms=1203 backend_error=kv-cache-timeout
[2026-03-15T22:14:03Z] request_id=abc124 route=/v1/generate status=503 duration_ms=98 upstream=transformer-oom
```

Raj Patel: looks like transformer instances in the canary pool are throwing OOM/restart cycles. k8s shows CrashLoopBackOff on 2/6 pods.
Marta Gomez: do we have a fast kill switch on the rollout?
Alice Chen: yes -- feature flag manager supports immediate rollback for traffic routing. command below to set traffic back to stable and disable experimental weights:
```
# set weight to 0 for canary
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  https://flags.redwood.internal/api/v1/traffic/rollouts/r2026-03-15-7f2a/actions \
  -d '{"action":"set_weight","target":"canary","weight":0}'
```

Alice Chen: I'm going to run that now. I'll also open a rollback in the release manager.
Alice Chen: RUN: set weight to 0 -> ok 200
eng-release-bot: Action accepted. Routing change propagated to edge in ~18s. Canary traffic reduced to 0.
Oncall-Bot: NOTE: abort criteria triggered and routing flag flipped by Alice Chen. Auto escalation suppressed.
Raj Patel: nice. let's monitor for error rate regression to stable baseline. running quick smoke against stable endpoint.
Alice Chen: smoke: /v1/health -> OK. /v1/generate (sample) -> 200, latency ~120ms. 5xx rate falling: 0.9% in last 2m.
Marta Gomez: good. do we want to start rollback of the canary build or hold it in place for postmortem?
Product-SRE: recommend rollback to previous stable image for the release and block re-rollout until root cause identified. high-visibility release.
Alice Chen: agreed. creating rollback ticket and kicking off a rolling revert.
eng-release-bot: Revert job queued: r2026-03-15-7f2a -> revert to r2026-03-08-stable. Estimated revert time 6m.
Raj Patel: tagging relevant folks: @product-sre, @release-eng. Also we should notify customer-facing teams: possible short window of 5xxs for small subset of customers.
Marta Gomez: product-sre -- any known config changes in this build (quantization, memory-tiling) that could explain OOM?
Product-SRE: yes this build included the new tiled-kernel path and a change in max_batch_size default from 8->12. that could raise memory pressure.
Raj Patel: that fits. set a follow-up to revert kernel flags and keep max_batch_size=8 for next try.
Alice Chen: Customer impact: checking error logs for customer ids. so far ~14 distinct customer sessions saw transient 503s, mostly short lived. two sessions for enterprise-cust-14 experienced disconnects during streaming; I've flagged for CS follow-up.
Marta Gomez: good catch. create post-incident notification draft for status page and ops slack for CS.
Alice Chen: drafting now. will include timeline, mitigation (flag flip + revert), and next steps (root cause: memory pressure from tiled-kernel + max_batch_size increase).
Alice Chen: we've suppressed paging to reduce noise, but keeping channel open for updates.
Oncall-Bot: handoff reminder: current oncall shift ends in 35m. please declare handoff if you won't be around.
Raj Patel: I'm available for handoff. I'll take the monitor until the revert is complete and do postmortem with release and infra tomorrow.
Marta Gomez: I'll own customer comms with CS and Sales for impacted customers; will post an incident summary after revert completes.
Alice Chen: thanks. I also kicked off a canary debug job to collect heap dumps from failed pods, saved to s3://redwood-incident-dumps/r2026-03-15-7f2a/ .
Raj Patel: adding note: runbook section 4.3 (canary OOM) suggests lowering batch size and disabling tiled-kernel before re-roll.
Alice Chen: scheduled follow-up: tomorrow 09:00 UTC postmortem w/ release, infra, and SRE.
Marta Gomez: posting to #statuspage: "Partial disruption for a small number of customers during canary rollout. Deployment traffic aborted and revert initiated. No ongoing service degradation. Investigating cause; follow-up to come."
Alice Chen: revert complete. eng-release-bot reports all pods stable on r2026-03-08-stable. 5xx rate holding at baseline.
eng-release-bot: Revert completed at 2487654360.
Alice Chen: closing immediate action. leaving notes in the rollback ticket with all artifacts (logs, heap dumps, decision timeline).
Raj Patel: taking over monitoring. oncall handoff done to Raj Patel.
Oncall-Bot: Handoff recorded: from Alice Chen to Raj Patel at 2487654375.
Alice Chen: thanks team. will add postmortem draft to epic and ping for reviews.
Marta Gomez: will follow up with CS and Sales on impacted sessions.
Product-SRE: will prepare a mitigation patch (revert kernel + lower default batch) and coordinate reschedule of the rollout after validation.
Alice Chen: end of thread.
